children: Hanover Insurance Group reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.74B, up 4.2% from a year earlier, while net income declined 3.4% to $172.6M and diluted EPS slipped to $4.86 from $4.9, primarily due to higher investment losses.
Revenue was $1.74B, compared with $1.67B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 4.2%.
Net income was $172.6M, compared with $178.7M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (3.4%).
Diluted EPS was $4.86, compared with $4.90 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (0.8%).
Nine-month net premiums written increased 3.6%, supported by renewal price increases and new business growth.
Core Commercial premiums written rose 5.3%; improved underlying underwriting results were partly offset by higher catastrophe losses.
Specialty premiums written grew 3.3%, alongside stronger underlying underwriting performance from lower current-year losses and earned-premium growth.
Personal Lines premiums written increased 2.3%, with lower current-year losses improving underlying results, while policies in force declined year over year.
The company said it remains focused on independent agents, disciplined underwriting, selective growth and rate increases where appropriate.
